records.body: A threat loses power once the consequence behind it is no longer enough to force compliance. When Pluto opposes Lilith, concentrated power meets a refusal that is no longer willing to pay the same price for access, approval, money, status, or peace. Questions of control become harder to ignore once the consequence is named plainly. What has been tolerated can become much harder to keep tolerating after the threat stops feeling absolute. The useful shift is the one that reduces the old source of control instead of turning resistance into another contest over who controls the terms.

records.summary: Power struggles become harder to contain when an old expectation of compliance stops working.
records.body: Power struggles become harder to contain when an old expectation of compliance stops working. When Pluto squares Lilith, the drive for control meets a refusal that is no longer willing to cooperate on the old terms. There may be far less tolerance for the unspoken rules about who gets to call the shots and who is expected to stay quiet. What has been tolerated for the sake of keeping the peace becomes harder to keep tolerating once the price is obvious. The pushback can be intense, but not every act of defiance needs to become a fight for total control.

previousReaderCopy.body: An obligation can look completely different once it becomes obvious that the arrangement works only because one person keeps absorbing the part nobody else wants. The commitment can still matter without every condition attached to it deserving to survive. The arrangement becomes more honest when responsibility is redistributed instead of hidden inside the person most accustomed to taking it.
